I've decided to take `mini.nvim` for a spin and thought I'd get everything setup however I am struggling with what seems to be keymaps being overwritten when using the `clue` submodule. As an example, through `lsp-zero` I should have access to `gd` (go to definition) however when I enable clue for the `g` key, that keymap no longer seems to function correctly. Below is my `mini.nvim` config and `lsp-zero` config respectively:

### mini.nvim
<details>

```lua
return {
  "echasnovski/mini.nvim",
  version = "*",
  keys = {
    { "<leader>l", ':lua MiniFiles.open()<cr>', desc = "File browser" },
  },
  lazy = false,
  dependencies = { "nvim-tree/nvim-web-devicons" },
  config = function()
    require("mini.pairs").setup({})
    require("mini.ai").setup({})
    require("mini.align").setup({})
    require("mini.bracketed").setup({})
    require("mini.comment").setup({})
    require("mini.files").setup({})
    require("mini.surround").setup({})

    local miniclue = require('mini.clue')
    miniclue.setup({
      triggers = {
        { mode = "n", keys = "<Leader>" },

        -- built-in completion
        { mode = "i", keys = "<C-x>" },

        -- `g` key
        { mode = 'n', keys = 'g' },
        { mode = 'x', keys = 'g' },

        -- Marks
        { mode = 'n', keys = "'" },
        { mode = 'n', keys = '`' },
        { mode = 'x', keys = "'" },
        { mode = 'x', keys = '`' },

        -- Registers
        { mode = 'n', keys = '"' },
        { mode = 'x', keys = '"' },
        { mode = 'i', keys = '<C-r>' },
        { mode = 'c', keys = '<C-r>' },

        -- Window commands
        { mode = 'n', keys = '<C-w>' },

        -- `z` key
        { mode = 'n', keys = 'z' },
        { mode = 'x', keys = 'z' },
      },

      clues = {
        -- Enhance this by adding descriptions for <Leader> mapping groups
        miniclue.gen_clues.builtin_completion(),
        miniclue.gen_clues.g(),
        miniclue.gen_clues.marks(),
        miniclue.gen_clues.registers(),
        miniclue.gen_clues.windows(),
        miniclue.gen_clues.z(),
      },

      window = {
        delay = 100,
        config = {
          width = "auto",
        }
      }
    })
  end
}
```

</details>

### lzp-zero

<details>

```lua
return {
  'VonHeikemen/lsp-zero.nvim',
  branch = 'v2.x',
  dependencies = {
    -- LSP Support
    { 'neovim/nvim-lspconfig' },             -- Required
    { 'williamboman/mason.nvim' },           -- Optional
    { 'williamboman/mason-lspconfig.nvim' }, -- Optional

    -- Autocompletion
    { 'hrsh7th/nvim-cmp' },     -- Required
    { 'hrsh7th/cmp-nvim-lsp' }, -- Required
    {
      "L3MON4D3/LuaSnip",
      version = "2.*",
      build = "make install_jsregexp",
      dependencies = {
        "rafamadriz/friendly-snippets",
        "andys8/vscode-jest-snippets",
      },
    },
    -- Extra cmp plugins
    { 'hrsh7th/cmp-buffer' },
    { 'hrsh7th/cmp-path' },
    { "hrsh7th/cmp-cmdline" },
  },
  config = function()
    local lsp = require('lsp-zero').preset({
      manage_nvim_cmp = {
        set_basic_mappings = true,
        set_extra_mappings = true,
      },
    })
    lsp.on_attach(function(_, bufnr)
      lsp.default_keymaps({ buffer = bufnr })
      lsp.buffer_autoformat()

      local bind = vim.keymap.set
      bind('n', '<leader>ca', vim.lsp.buf.code_action, { buffer = bufnr, desc = "Code actions" })
      bind("n", "<C-k>", vim.lsp.buf.signature_help, { buffer = bufnr, desc = "Signature help" })
      bind("n", "<leader>D", vim.lsp.buf.type_definition, { buffer = bufnr, desc = "Type definition" })
      bind("n", "<leader>rn", vim.lsp.buf.rename, { buffer = bufnr, desc = "Rename" })
    end)

    -- lsp for neovim
    require('lspconfig').lua_ls.setup(lsp.nvim_lua_ls())

    lsp.setup()
    local cmp = require('cmp')
    local cmp_action = require('lsp-zero').cmp_action()

    require('luasnip.loaders.from_vscode').lazy_load()
    require("luasnip").filetype_extend("typescript", { "javascript", "tsdoc", "js" })

    cmp.setup({
      sources = {
        { name = "codeium" },
        { name = 'nvim_lsp' },
        { name = 'luasnip' },
        { name = 'buffer' },
        { name = 'path' },
        { name = 'nvim_lua' },
      },
      mapping = {
        ['<C-f>'] = cmp_action.luasnip_jump_forward(),
        ['<C-b>'] = cmp_action.luasnip_jump_backward(),
        ['<CR>']  = cmp.mapping.confirm({ select = false }),
      },
    })

    -- Use buffer source for `/` and `?`.
    cmp.setup.cmdline({ "/", "?" }, {
      mapping = cmp.mapping.preset.cmdline(),
      sources = {
        { name = "buffer" },
      },
    })

    -- Use cmdline & path source for ':'.
    cmp.setup.cmdline(":", {
      mapping = cmp.mapping.preset.cmdline(),
      sources = cmp.config.sources({
        { name = "path" },
      }, {
        { name = "cmdline" },
      }),
    })
  end,
}
```

</details>

If I comment out this section, then `gd` works as expected however I obviously lose the clues for `g`

```lua
        -- `g` key
        { mode = 'n', keys = 'g' },
        { mode = 'x', keys = 'g' },
```

How can I fix or troubleshoot this?

comment_data.body:
Unfortunately, it is an issue of 'mini.clue' design: it defines triggers as buffer local mappings which **need** to be defined last in the buffer. When you use `lsp.on_attach`, it creates buffer-local mappings after `g` trigger is created.

Fortunately, it is a **known** issue with [this suggested solution approach](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/707dca4f4152c2d9c9b4c5e02635f78dfd33db50/doc/mini-clue.txt#L60-L77).

On a side note, this is slightly strange, because 'mini.clue' should [account for LSP attaching](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/lua/mini/clue.lua#L1184).

title: [mini.clue] Clue mappings override LSP mappings
